correctness.rationale: The independent linear forms M_ij can be completed to a linear basis with f=d(3d-1)/2 free coordinates. Under the explicitly stated level-two shuffle identities M_ij=v_i v_j, elimination gives C[v_i v_j,z], the second Veronese invariant algebra. Standard pair-switching straightening proves the prime defining ideal is all symmetric 2x2 minors; its dimension d+f, degree 2^{d-1}, Hilbert numerator Σ_j binom(d,2j)t^j, and singular locus M=0 follow. The principal-only ideal comprises E=binom(d,2) independent quadrics with pairwise coprime off-diagonal leading squares, so is complete intersection and CM; on the dense nonzero-diagonal torus every irreducible signed component is generically smooth, giving reducedness. Vertex-sign gauge has 2^{E-d+1} orbits, each signed rank-one cone degree 2^{d-1}; their degrees sum to 2^E. An explicit 3x3 matrix has every principal minor zero but nonprincipal minor −2 and determinant −4, distinguishing loci for all d≥3, while they coincide d=2. All degree claims restricted to complex homogeneous level two; source-paper shuffle identity itself deserves comparison with the primary original.
